reason: The cited lines show the handler validates params, sends a fixed socket message to perform a browser hover, then captures and returns the browser page URL, title, and ARIA snapshot. This does not show arbitrary host code execution. It does not show delivery to an attacker-readable or agent-chosen destination; the socket messages are to the browser/context. The returned page URL/title/snapshot are browser page content and can be controlled by a web page, so UNTRUSTED is supported. The lines show page content being returned, but do not by themselves establish that the page is non-public, credentialed SaaS, localhost, file, or intranet content, so SECRET is insufficient.
